q: How much energy does the Thangadh sanitaryware cluster use, and what is CO2 per tonne of ware?
title: Thangadh sanitaryware: energy and CO2 a tonne
short: In 2009 the cluster used 33,644 toe a year, 83% of it natural gas, and averaged 0.091 toe and 0.27 t CO2 per tonne of product. Sanitaryware units ranged from 0.074 to 0.105 toe per tonne. Recalculated on today's factors, the cluster's fossil CO2 comes to about 0.22 t per tonne.
audience: Sanitaryware, refractory and tile units in Thangadh, Surendranagar district, and the brands and distributors they supply

ul: About 225 ceramic units: 161 sanitaryware, 45 refractories, 11 art ware and 8 wall tile.
By size: 50 small (1 to 4 tonnes a day), 100 medium (4 to 8) and 75 large (above 8).
Energy is 30 to 35% of production cost. Most wall and floor tile units have closed; sanitaryware and refractories carry the cluster.
Kilns fire ware at about 1,200 degrees C. Many tunnel kilns still used kerosene burners, and units had been moving to gas since it arrived about two years before the study.

sections.h: The cluster's CO2 on today's factors
ul: Gas: 33 million scm x 2.05 kg = 67,650 t.
Electricity: 18 million kWh x 0.675 kg = 12,150 t.
Fossil total: about 80,750 t on about 370,000 t of product (33,644 toe at 0.091 toe per tonne), roughly 0.22 t per tonne. Charcoal CO2 is biogenic and reported separately.

p: The study put the cluster's saving potential at 8,800 toe a year: kiln heat recovery, better insulation and gas burners in place of kerosene burners (about 15%), lighter kiln cars (about 10% of tunnel kiln energy), and efficient motors and controls in slip preparation (about 15% of power).

example.title: Worked example: a medium unit's month, against the cluster
lines: Kiln gas: 13,500 scm x 2.05 = 27.7 t CO2
Total 33.5 t for 150 t of good ware fired: 0.22 t CO2 per tonne
Cluster 2009: 0.27 t per tonne as reported; about 0.22 recalculated on today's factors. This unit sits at the cluster average
example.note: The month's quantities are an example. Count gas for rejected pieces in the total, but only good ware in the tonnes.

senseible: Senseible reads your gas, power and diesel bills each month into CO2 records; divide by tonnes of good ware fired for a figure you can set against the cluster's here, without building a spreadsheet of bills.
